purpose: Olmesartan is used to treat high blood pressure, also called hypertension. Keeping your blood pressure under control helps protect your heart, kidneys, and blood vessels. It can be used alone or together with other blood pressure medicines.
how_it_works: Your body makes a chemical called angiotensin II that tightens your blood vessels and raises your blood pressure. Olmesartan blocks the place where that chemical tries to attach, so your blood vessels relax and open up. This makes it easier for your heart to pump blood and brings your blood pressure down to a healthier level.
common_side_effects: Dizziness, especially when you stand up quickly. You may also notice headache, tiredness, an upset stomach, or mild diarrhea. Some people experience back pain or cold-like symptoms such as a runny nose.
warnings: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm your unborn baby. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems. Avoid taking potassium supplements or salt substitutes without asking your doctor first. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor. In rare cases, especially in people with celiac disease, this medicine can cause severe diarrhea and significant weight loss — tell your doctor right away if this happens.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 20 mg taken by mouth once a day. Your doctor may increase your dose to 40 mg once a day if your blood pressure is not well controlled after 2 weeks. Take it at the same time each day, with or without food. Try not to miss doses.
